title: Daily Market Digest: November 02, 2026
subtitle: US Equities End Lower as Tech Weakness Persists; Oil Prices Fall

items.headline: US Equities Conclude Lower as Tech Sector Weighs, Despite Early Rally
items.summary: U.S. stocks finished Monday's session in negative territory, driven by continued selling pressure in mega-cap technology and semiconductor stocks. This occurred despite an initial market rally spurred by easing oil prices, which fell on hopes for a diplomatic resolution in the Middle East. The overall market sentiment reflects persistent concerns over AI investment returns and the upcoming midterm elections. Not financial advice.

items.statContext: Tumbled 2.00% as tech and semiconductor stocks faced significant selling.

items.headline: IDEXX Laboratories Inc. Rallies
items.summary: Veterinary diagnostic company IDEXX Laboratories Inc. ($IDXX) saw a significant jump in early trading.

items.headline: EVgo Surges on Acquisition Proposal
items.summary: Electric vehicle charging network EVgo ($EVGO) climbed significantly following a $2.00 per share cash proposal.

items.headline: Once Upon a Farm Tumbles Post-Recall
items.summary: Organic food company Once Upon a Farm experienced a sharp decline after announcing a recall of a toddler snack bar.

items.headline: Oil Prices Plummet Amid Hopes for US-Iran Diplomatic Resolution
items.summary: Global crude oil benchmarks fell sharply today, with Brent crude dropping 5.9% to $106.65, on optimism surrounding potential diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran. Iran announced a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear discussions, easing supply disruption fears and boosting risk sentiment in the broader market.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Maintains Key Interest Rate Ahead of Jobs Data
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held its federal funds target range steady at 3-3/4 to 4 percent in a 10-2 vote last week, with inflation remaining elevated. Investors are now looking ahead to federal labor data and the Treasury Department's quarterly refunding announcement later this week.

items.headline: Tech Sector Continues to Grapple with AI Spending Concerns Post-Earnings
items.summary: The technology sector remained under pressure as concerns mounted over whether massive investments in AI infrastructure will yield sufficient returns. This follows disappointing quarterly results and lower-than-expected AI spending forecasts from major tech players like Amazon, Alphabet, and Intel last week, contributing to a significant tech sell-off.

items.headline: Marriott Reports Strong Q3 Earnings, Raises Full-Year Outlook
items.summary: Marriott International posted robust third-quarter results, with adjusted earnings of $3.02 per share, surpassing analyst expectations of $2.84. Revenue climbed 8% to $7.005 billion, also beating estimates. The company raised its full-year 2026 global RevPAR growth outlook to a range of 4.5% to 5%.

items.headline: Midterm Elections Loom, Investors Eye Potential Policy Shifts
items.summary: With U.S. midterm elections scheduled for November 3, market participants are closely monitoring the political landscape. The outcome could significantly influence fiscal policy, government borrowing, and Treasury yields, adding a layer of uncertainty to the market outlook.
